Research record / Preprint

LUXVAR: A Constructed Language with Distinctive Morphemic Structure and AI-Recoverable Morpheme Families

The strongest supported reading is morphemic and phonotactic structure, not independent recovery of the designed semantic axes. The August addendum explicitly rejects the “AI-recoverable” axis reading.

v2.22026-08-26ZenodoPreprint
Evidence status

Mixed: reproducible morphology/phonotactics results plus negative semantic-axis tests; the historical “AI-recoverable” title claim is rejected by the paper’s later addendum. Publication status: Preprint; explicitly marked not peer-reviewed in the deposited manuscript.

01 / question

Research question and current reading.

Research question

Which parts of LUXVAR’s designed structure are recoverable computationally, and do those recoverable regularities extend from morphology and clustering to the intended semantic axes?

The strongest supported reading is morphemic and phonotactic structure, not independent recovery of the designed semantic axes. The August addendum explicitly rejects the “AI-recoverable” axis reading.

02 / methods

What was actually tested.

  • Morphological clustering over 801 roots with 36 phonotactic features and shuffle baselines.
  • GEN-001 random-forest phonotactic classification using 34 features and five-fold cross-validation.
  • GEN-003R+ cross-language benchmark against six curated lexical corpora with balanced n = 107 and bootstrap uncertainty.
  • SEM-001 string-level and SEM-002 graph-level semantic-axis tests.
  • VPE-001B+ independent AI clustering of Core-30, scored against both inter-model agreement and the designed axes.
03 / results

Strongest supported findings.

  • Non-random morphology: z = 4.36, p < 0.001; silhouette 0.406 versus shuffled mean 0.174.
  • Generator balance at n = 2,000,000: H/Hmax = 0.9995 and Cramér’s V < 0.02 for the stated first-order associations.
  • Phonotactic distinctiveness: GEN-001 CV accuracy 98.9%; uniqueness = 0.738, 95% CI [0.703, 0.781], versus six curated reference language lists.
  • Claude↔Gemini inter-model cluster ARI is reported as 0.812 in the corrected manuscript, but mean ARI versus the designed axes is 0.150; the later addendum rejects interpreting inter-model agreement as axis recovery.
04 / scale & benchmark lineage

How this experiment relates to Core-30 and later scaled benchmarks.

Core-30

30 reference words

Canonical public reference subset used in several early clustering/audit tasks; it remains a reference set rather than the whole LUXVAR system.

Broader LUXVAR design

801 stable roots

The v2.2 manuscript reports 801 stable roots across six semantic fields and other generator dimensions. Core-30 separately uses five designed axes; the relationship is retained as a source-level distinction, not silently harmonized.

Generated corpus

≈1.3 billion generated forms

Exhaustive combinations of the manuscript’s design dimensions. The rows are generated by construction, not observations collected from natural language use.

Scale boundary: Core-30 remains a canonical reference subset. Larger generated corpora and later benchmark datasets are distinct experimental artifacts and should not be silently relabeled as a single enlarged canonical lexicon.

05 / falsification

Negative findings are part of the result.

  • Hexacore k = 6 was rejected; the reported natural elbow was k = 3.
  • SEM-001 found no semantic-axis string signal; SEM-002 reached only 1/4 positive tests against a ≥2/4 criterion.
  • Root→field and root→frequency first-order signals were not found under the stated thresholds.
  • The August 2026 addendum explicitly marks the “AI-Recoverable” claim as REJECTED after direct axis-label testing in the companion Track D audit.
06 / limits

What this record does not establish.

  • Reference-language comparisons use curated lexical lists rather than large natural-text corpora.
  • AI clustering is not a human perception study; VPE-001A remained unperformed in this manuscript.
  • Frequency values are symbolic design parameters, not experimentally validated physical or cognitive categories.
  • LUXVAR is a single-creator constructed system; semantic-axis inter-rater validity had not been established.
  • Taxonomy provenance: Core-30 is described with five designed axes, while the wider v2.2 layer is described with six semantic fields; the public site preserves this documentary distinction rather than assuming equivalence.

Boundary: a Zenodo deposit is a citable public record; it does not by itself imply peer review, independent validation, causal inference, or generalization beyond the documented experiment.

10 / version provenance

Keep this deposit distinct from later interpretation.

The record provides a clear separation between designed structure, computationally detectable morpheme-family organization, and the stronger semantic claim that the intended axes are independently recoverable. The latter is not treated as established.

Version v2.2 is the current public LUXVAR record listed by VARZIN. The historical title wording is retained for citation continuity even where later interpretation is more conservative.
